skill.name: ux-waiting-audit
skill.description: Audit waiting states for web applications with long-running operations. The skill guides browser-based screenshot capture, checklist scoring, and prioritized UX recommendations for loading, progress, and completion states.
skill.summary: Audits loading and waiting UX for long-running web operations.
skill.author: BayramAnnakov

security_audit.summary: The README URL and Claude home-directory path are documentation examples, and the markdown fence alerts are false positives rather than OS command execution. The screen-capture upload alerts are also false positives because the cited lines describe user-directed screenshots without an upload destination. I confirmed one high-severity semantic issue: the skill asks for login credentials when authentication is needed.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the request for login credentials. Ask users to authenticate in their browser session or provide a non-production test account.
Add instructions to avoid production personal data in screenshots and to redact reports before sharing them outside the audit team.
State that audits should run only on systems the user owns or has permission to test, with no destructive interactions.

content.user_title: Audit Waiting UX in Web Apps
content.value_statement: Long-running web operations can make users abandon tasks when progress is unclear. This skill guides screenshot-based audits with checklists and prioritized recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Guides browser navigation to a target web application before testing a long-running operation.
Captures screenshots at T+0, T+10, T+30, and completion points.
Checks for spinners, progress bars, status text, partial results, and completion signals.
Scores waiting states against a ten-point UX checklist.
Produces a report with strengths, gaps, quick wins, and priority recommendations.
limitations: Requires browser automation access and a reachable web application.
Protected flows may require the user to authenticate manually before testing.
Screenshots can contain sensitive data and need careful handling.
Does not replace usability testing with real users.

use_cases.title: Improve AI Task Feedback
use_cases.description: Review how an AI product explains work during 30 to 60 second operations and identify better progress signals.

use_cases.title: Validate Loading Patterns
use_cases.description: Check whether a web app shows useful status, partial results, cancellation, and completion feedback during slow flows.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Findings
use_cases.description: Create a prioritized waiting-state report before shipping a feature with report generation, search, export, or deployment delays.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Waiting Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the waiting UX on this URL. I will tell you the operation to trigger and the expected wait time.

prompt_templates.title: Authenticated Flow Review
prompt_templates.prompt: After I authenticate in the browser, audit the waiting states for this protected workflow and report the main UX gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Checklist Scoring Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this long-running operation against the ten-point waiting UX checklist and provide a score with prioritized fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Comparative Wait Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Capture the start, middle, and completion states for this operation, then compare activity signals, anxiety risks, and interruption options.

output_examples.input: A 45 second report generation flow with a spinner and no status text.
output_examples.output: The report identifies missing time estimation, weak heartbeat signals, and no cancellation option. It recommends status text, progress milestones, and partial-result previews.

output_examples.input: An AI research workflow that streams partial findings during a long wait.
output_examples.output: The audit highlights strong progressive value and completion feedback. It recommends clearer remaining-time language and better recovery messaging for partial failures.

output_examples.input: A deployment page with logs, progress steps, and final success feedback.
output_examples.output: The output compares each timeline screenshot, scores the checklist, and separates quick wins from deeper product changes.

best_practices: Use test accounts and non-production data when auditing authenticated flows.
Capture the same operation at consistent timeline points for fair comparison.
Pair visual screenshots with simple state checks for progress, text, and result changes.
anti_patterns: Do not ask users to paste production passwords or private tokens into the chat.
Do not rely only on DOM selectors when screenshots show a different visual state.
Do not treat a spinner alone as sufficient feedback for long waits.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits loading and waiting states for web operations that take about 30 seconds or longer.

faq.question: Does it need browser automation?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed for browser-based inspection with screenshots and simple page-state checks.

faq.question: Can it test authenticated pages?
faq.answer: Yes, but users should authenticate directly in the browser or use test accounts. They should not share real credentials.

faq.question: What output should users expect?
faq.answer: Users should expect a timeline review, checklist score, strengths, gaps, quick wins, and prioritized recommendations.

faq.question: Is this a performance testing tool?
faq.answer: No. It evaluates the user experience of waiting, not backend speed or infrastructure performance.

faq.question: How should screenshots be handled?
faq.answer: Screenshots should use safe test data when possible and be redacted before sharing outside the audit group.
